verdict.rationale: ROS 2 ships its own SDK surface: multi-language client libraries plus topics, services and actions for sending goals to a robot. It also ships SROS2/DDS-Security, which authenticates participants and applies per-enclave policies that can be mapped to processes, users or devices, a form of scoped credential. Nothing in the evidence shows AI-agent-oriented integration or a documented end-to-end real-robot agent workflow, so the agent part of the story rests on generic client-library use. missing for 10: agent-specific integration or tooling, documented end-to-end real-robot command workflow, hands-on corroboration of secured agent control.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an AI agent authenticate with scoped credentials and command a real robot end-to-end through the platform's API or SDK

citations.quote: Client libraries come in a variety of programming languages so that users may write ROS 2 code in the language that is best-suited for their application.

Security enclaves can be flexibly mapped to processes, users, or devices at deployment.
